stated: Legislate to ensure there is a parliamentary vote before engaging in military action, and support intervention only when there is a clear legal or humanitarian case, while preserving the government’s ability to engage in action in emergencies with a retrospective vote or under treaty obligation.

source.quote: Legislate to ensure there is a parliamentary vote before engaging in military action, and support intervention only when there is a clear legal or humanitarian case, while preserving the government’s ability to engage in action in emergencies with a retrospective vote or under treaty obligation.

bearing_set.reason: Legislating a pre-action parliamentary vote directly alters the UK's defence and national security decision-making process, affecting the speed, legitimacy, and circumstances under which military force can be deployed — a real verdict on defence posture and security.

Requiring a statutory parliamentary vote before committing to military action directly advances democratic rights and due process over a major exercise of executive power, a clear O9 indicator ('voting & democratic rights', 'due process & rule of law').

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O5 (the security/defence-posture effect of constraining when military action can be taken) and O9 (the democratic-accountability effect of legislating parliamentary oversight of that power). No material bearing on personal liberty (O10), public finances (O12), or other fundamentals — the policy is procedural/constitutional in scope, not fiscal or social.
